title: Mastering Pupillary Block Glaucoma: Pathophysiology to Management
summary: Pupillary block glaucoma is the most common form of angle-closure glaucoma, occurring when resistance to aqueous humor flow through the pupil leads to iris bombe and acute obstruction of the trabecular meshwork. Urgent identification and mechanical relief of this block are essential to prevent irreversible optic nerve damage.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Pupillary block is the obstruction of aqueous flow from the posterior chamber to the anterior chamber through the pupil. This pressure differential causes the iris to bow anteriorly (iris bombe), pushing the peripheral iris into the trabecular meshwork, leading to secondary angle closure. The hallmark is the iris-lens contact at the pupillary margin.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation: Red Flags
content: Severe ocular pain and peri-orbital headache
Nausea and vomiting (vagal response to pain)

rows: Deepening of peripheral AC but shallow central AC
Hypermature cataract with lens protein leak

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (assess AC depth, iris bombe)
Step 2: Gonioscopy (Gold standard for angle assessment - Shafer grading)
Step 4: UBM or Anterior Segment OCT (Visualize iris-lens contact)
Step 5: Fundoscopy (Assess disc cupping, if corneal clarity permits)

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Immediate IOP reduction (Topical timolol, apraclonidine, pilocarpine 1-2% after IOP < 40 mmHg)
Step 2: Systemic therapy (IV Acetazolamide 500mg or Oral Mannitol)
Step 3: Laser Peripheral Iridotomy (LPI) - definitive treatment once cornea clears
Step 4: Phacoemulsification if cataract is significant or LPI fails to open angle

content.explanation: P: Painful eye, U: Unilateral/Unrelenting, P: Pressure high, I: Iris bombe, L: LPI is curative

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Never perform pilocarpine while IOP > 40-50 mmHg (ischemic sphincter paralysis).
Always perform gonioscopy on the fellow eye; 50% risk of closure in 5 years.
LPI location: 11 or 1 o'clock to allow eyelid coverage.
Plateau iris syndrome: suspect if angle remains closed after LPI.
